symptoms: Small circular to elongated golden-brown to cinnamon pustules (uredinia) on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture epidermal tissue, releasing powdery rust-colored spores
Pustules darken to brown or black later in the season as teliospores form
management: Prioritize resistant hybrids suited for your agro-ecological altitude.
Do not apply fungicides indiscriminately; common rust rarely causes severe yield loss on mature plants in Kenya unless onset is very early (pre-tassel).
Seek advice from Sub-county Agricultural Extension Officers before making chemical fungicide purchases.
prevention: Use KEPHIS-certified rust-tolerant maize hybrid seed suitable for cool/moist highland zones.
Maintain balanced soil fertility according to soil test recommendations.
Maintain clean field borders and eradicate alternative host weeds (such as Oxalis species) around field edges.
monitoring: Inspect leaves on both sides during cool (16-24°C) and moist conditions typical of early morning dews.
Monitor whether pustules appear on upper leaves before the silking stage.
escalation: Pustules develop extensively across upper leaves prior to tasseling.
Severe leaf necrosis and chlorosis covering more than 20% of canopy during reproductive stages.
Cold, foggy highland weather prolongs free leaf moisture.
kenya_notes: Common in cooler highland regions (Central Highlands, Rift Valley highlands, Kisii, Western highlands). Yield impact is highest when cool, damp weather occurs early in the vegetative cycle.
